name: Apollo Tyres Ltd
about: India's second-largest tyre maker by revenue after MRF, with a European arm (Apollo Vredestein: the premium Vredestein brand, a plant at Gyöngyöshalász, Hungary, R&D at Enschede, Netherlands, and the ReifenCom distribution business in Germany). Five Indian plants (Perambra and Kalamassery in Kerala, Limda in Gujarat, Chennai, Chinnapandur in Andhra Pradesh) and Hungary; sells in 100+ countries. Products: truck-bus (radial TBR and bias), passenger car (PCR), light truck, farm, two-wheeler and off-highway tyres.

callPoints: India revenue +15.6% (volume ~+12%), the strongest growth in 14 quarters; replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15%; every category but bias truck tyres grew double digits. July 'a strong start' (CFO, 7-Aug-2026).
Raw materials +17% q/q in Q1 (rubber ~Rs225/kg) and +8% more expected in Q2 (rubber Rs260+/kg); about half of raw materials are imported and the rupee's fall added 7-8%.

Price increases: ~11-12% needed for Q1's cost, 7-9% taken (only 3-4% visible in Q1 revenue); with Q2's cost the need is 15-16% vs ~11% taken. 1-2% in July, ~2% expected in August; OEM formula prices follow with a quarter's lag.

Europe: revenue EUR147 mn (+0.5%), EBITDA margin 8.9% (10.8%); ~11% without the overlap of Enschede and Hungary costs; Enschede stopped production in Jun-2026 and the benefits start in H2FY27; 'high teens' EBITDA is the full-year aim once the footprint is right.
Agri tyres made at Enschede: no equivalent capacity elsewhere; 20-25% of Europe's agri business now comes from two offtake partners; 'a couple of quarters' to stabilise.
Capacity: India running 'into the 90s', tight all FY27; Hungary PCR 17,000 to 21,000 tyres a day from H2FY27; Andhra Pradesh expansion from end-FY27, ramping through FY28.
Capex Rs650 cr in Q1 (India Rs500 cr); FY27 ~Rs3,000 cr (MOSL); 'we will be a net borrower'; net debt ~Rs1,700 cr, 0.4x EBITDA.
Advertising and sales promotion cut ~50% in Q1 after the Q4 BCCI jersey activation; not expected to fall further.
Market share (internal estimates): TBR replacement 30%+ (regained), PCR replacement 21%+.
CFO Gaurav Kumar announced his resignation on the call after 22 years at Apollo; MD Neeraj Kanwar did not attend.

enschede.timeline: Request for Advice to the Works Council 25-Apr-2025; settlement Sep-2025; production stopped 30-Jun-2026; capacity moved to Hungary (most PCR), India (14-15 inch tyres; Spacemaster spare tyres to Vadodara) and offtake partners (high-end agri).
enschede.volume: ~750,000 tyres sold from the plant in FY26 (CFO, Q1FY27 call)
enschede.charges: FY25 Rs128 cr impairment; FY26 Rs1,000 cr (restructuring Rs545 cr, impairment and closure costs Rs455 cr, incl. a EUR43 mn fixed-asset write-off in Q4)
enschede.cash: ~EUR55 mn+ of cash provisions (EUR50 mn social plan plus legal and other costs) to be paid in FY27; already provided (CFO, Q4FY26 call)
enschede.agriShare: Agri ~12% of Europe revenue, half of it OE (loss-making, may be dropped)
enschede.why: European market flat to negative for two years; Dutch salaries up 12-13% over two-three years vs 4-5% normal; energy costs (CFO, Q4FY26 call)
enschede.benefit: From H2FY27; Europe margin ~11% in Q1 without overlap costs; 16%+ 'earlier normal', high teens aspiration
